'''Ricola Ltd.'''/'''Ricola''' '''AG''' is a [[Switzerland|Swiss]] manufacturer of [[Throat lozenge|cough drop]]s, [[instant tea]], tea bags, and [[Mint (candy)|breath mint]]s. The head office of Ricola is located in [[Laufen, Switzerland|Laufen]], Basel-Country,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ricola.com/en-ch/Meta/Contact |title=Contact |work=Ricola |publisher=Ricola AG |accessdate=2015-12-02}}</ref> and has subsidiaries in [[Italy]], [[Great Britain]], [[Asia]], and the [[United States]]. According to the company, it exports to around 45 countries in Europe, Asia, and North America.

==Business==
Ricola is a family business owned by the Richterich family; the Chairman of the Board of Directors is Felix Richterich. At the end of November 2011, he also took over the position of managing director<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-11-25 |title=Ricola-Geschäftsleiter Adrian Kohler gestorben |url=https://www.bazonline.ch/ricola-geschaeftsleiter-adrian-kohler-gestorben-522224866606 |access-date=2023-05-25 |website=Basler Zeitung |language=de}}</ref> until he was replaced by Thomas P. Meier in May 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2019-05-22 |title=Ricola steigert Umsatz und stellt sich für die Zukunft neu auf |url=https://www.moneycab.com/schweiz/ricola-steigert-umsatz-und-stellt-sich-fuer-die-zukunft-neu-auf/ |access-date=2023-05-25 |website=Moneycab |language=de-CH}}</ref> Since then, the operational management of Ricola Group AG has been entirely in the hands of executives who do not belong to the owning family.<ref>{{Cite web |title=gfm-Marketing-Check mit Thomas P. Meier, CEO Ricola Group |url=https://gfm.ch/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Meier_Thomas_Marketingcheck.pdf |access-date=2023-05-25}}</ref>

From 2014 to the end of 2018, Eva Richterich, daughter of Alfred Richterich, was Vice President of the Board of Directors of Ricola. Eva Richterich left the Board of Directors at the end of 2018 when she joined the management of Ricola Group AG. At the end of 2020, Eva Richterich left Group Management and devoted herself to her strategic role as a member of the Board of Directors of Ricola Familienholding AG.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-12-17 |title=Neues Modell der Unternehmensführung bei Ricola |url=https://www.presseportal.ch/de/pm/100005111/100861985 |access-date=2023-05-25 |website=presseportal.ch |language=de}}</ref> After several years in operational management, Raphael Richterich, son of Felix Richterich and representative of the fourth generation of the family, was elected to the Board of Directors of Ricola Group AG in 2018, becoming Vice President in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-01-21 |title=Neuer Chef für Ricola |url=https://www.schweizerbauer.ch/markt-preise/marktmeldungen/neuer-chef-fuer-ricola/ |access-date=2023-05-25 |website=Schweizer Bauer |language=de-DE}}</ref>

Ricola is a member of the {{Lang|de|Interessengemeinschaft Tee, Gewürze und verwandte Produkte|italic=no}} (Interest Group for Tea, Spices, and Related Products; IGTG).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Unsere Mitgliedsfirmen |url=https://www.teeundgewuerze.ch/mitglieder/ |access-date=2024-07-07 |website=IGTG - Interessengemeinschaft Tee, Gewürze und verwandte Produkte |language=de}}</ref>

Ricola listed sales of 307.2 million [[Swiss franc]]s in 2016 and employs 400 workers. Around 200 independent production companies in the surrounding area service Ricola. In order to obtain enough [[herb]]s for the production of its herbal drops, the firm contracts over 100 self-managed farms in the [[Valais]], [[Emmental]], [[Val Poschiavo]] and at the southern foot of the [[Jura Mountains]], in central Switzerland, and in [[Ticino]]. Ricola is known for its commercials featuring Heidi ([[Ramona Pringle]]) depicting mountaineers shouting "Ri-co-la!" and blowing through a large [[Alphorn]]. 

A class action suit in February 2019 alleged non-natural ingredients ([[malic acid]], [[aspartame]], [[citric acid]], [[sorbitol]], [[ascorbic acid]], [[sodium ascorbate]]) while labels say "Naturally Soothing" or "Naturally Helps Support Immune System".<ref name="roch">{{Cite news |url=https://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/news/local/columnists/andreatta/2019/02/08/rochester-lawsuit-steuben-county-woman-amy-comfort-sues-ricola-cough-drop-company/2803481002/ |title=Andreatta: Steuben County woman wants Ricola to cough up $5 million |last=Andreatta |first=David |date=2019-02-08 |work=Rochester Democrat and Chronicle |access-date=2019-12-24 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="cl2019">{{Cite web |url=https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/14557210/comfort-v-ricola-usa-inc/ |title=Docket for Comfort v. Ricola USA, Inc., 6:19-cv-06089-CJS - CourtListener.com |website=CourtListener |language=en-us |access-date=2019-12-24}}</ref> In November 2019 the judge dismissed two claims and let two claims proceed.<ref name="cl2019b">{{Cite web |url=https://www.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nywd.121745/gov.uscourts.nywd.121745.16.0.pdf |title=DECISION AND ORDER |last=Siragusa |first=Charles |date=2019-11-14 |website=CourtListener |access-date=2019-12-24}}</ref> An earlier class action suit in November 2015 alleged industrially synthesized ingredients were used (ascorbic acid, citric acid, and malic acid) while labels stated "Naturally Soothing".<ref name="ln">{{Cite news |url=https://legalnewsline.com/stories/510650102-ricola-faces-class-action-suit-over-false-advertising-claims |title=Ricola faces class-action suit over false advertising claims |last=Hargett |first=Robbie |date=2015-11-30 |work=Legal Newsline |access-date=2019-12-24 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="cl2015">{{Cite web |url=https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/13247796/minker-v-ricola-usa-inc/ |title=Docket for Minker v. Ricola USA, Inc., 1:15-cv-09014 - CourtListener.com |website=CourtListener |language=en-us |access-date=2019-12-24}}</ref>
The suit was withdrawn without explanation in January 2016.<ref name="cl2016">{{Cite web |url=https://www.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.450065/gov.uscourts.nysd.450065.14.0.pdf |title=Notice of Dismissal, Case 1:15-cv-09014-RA Document 14 Filed 01/15/16 |date=2016-01-15 |website=CourtListener |access-date=2019-12-24}}</ref>

==History==
Ricola began in 1930 when master baker Emil Wilhelm Richterich and Daniel Ruoss Sr. established '''Confiseriefabrik Richterich & Co. Laufen''' after the purchase of a small bakery in his birthplace [[Laufen, Switzerland|Laufen]], just outside [[Basel]]. Under Richterich, the bakery specialized in confectionery such as {{Lang|de|Fünfermocken}}, a sweet similar to caramel. In 1940 Richterich experimented with the healing power of herbs and created Ricola's Swiss Herbal Sweet incorporating a blend of 13 herbs, which remains almost unchanged today.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Meske |first=Mara |title=Natur ist für mich die Welt |chapter=Die Lebenswelt von Kindern heute |publisher=VS Verlag für Sozialwissenschaften |year=2011 |pages=51–84 |isbn=978-3-531-17904-9 |location=Wiesbaden |doi=10.1007/978-3-531-92760-2_3 |lang=de}}</ref> In the 1950s the sweet became appreciated for its ability to be dissolved in boiling water, creating an aromatic [[herbal tea]] or tisane, which inspired Richterich to create a Ricola Herbal Tea a few years later.<ref name=hist>{{cite web |url=http://www.ricola.com/en-ch/About-Ricola/Company/History |title=History |work=Ricola |publisher=Ricola AG |accessdate=2015-12-02}}</ref>

In 1967, Emil Richterich and his sons Hans Peter and Alfred renamed the company '''Ricola''', an abbreviation of '''Ri'''chterich & '''Co'''mpagnie '''La'''ufen. Export began in the 1970s, introducing Ricola's products to foreign markets in [[Japan]], [[Hong Kong]], [[Singapore]], and the [[United States]]. At the end of the decade, Ricola moved to a new purpose-built factory in the vicinity of Laufen, where its headquarters are still located.<ref name=hist/>

In 1976, after extensive research on sugar-free confectionery, Ricola launched Switzerland’s first chewable sugarless herbal sweet. Ricola first started to advertise its products on television in the 1980s, an era that saw increased awareness of the need for good dental hygiene, increasing the demand for sugar-free products such as the ones that Ricola offered. In 1985, the cooperation with Swiss farmers for the natural cultivation of herbs according to [[Bio Suisse]] standards began.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Unsere Wurzeln |url=https://www.ricola.com/de/ricola/unternehmen/geschichte |access-date=2023-05-25}}</ref> The [[Klosterfrau Melissengeist|Klosterfrau Healthcare Group]] has been responsible for the distribution of Ricola products in Germany since 1987.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-10-03 |title=Ricola – Die hochwertigen Kräuterspezialitäten aus der Schweiz. |url=http://www.klosterfrau.de/marken/ricolar.html |access-date=2023-05-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171003201758/http://www.klosterfrau.de/marken/ricolar.html |archive-date=2017-10-03 }}</ref> In 1988 the company started packaging their products in small boxes.<ref name=hist/> In 2019, sales in Germany switched to CFP Brands, a joint venture in which Ricola participated.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ricola setzt künftig auf CFP Brands statt Klosterfrau |url=https://www.markenartikel-magazin.de/_rubric/detail.php?rubric=marke-marketing&nr=20237 |access-date=2023-06-01 |website=www.markenartikel-magazin.de |language=de-DE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Distribution joint venture CFP Brands |url=https://www.ricola.com/en/about/media/press-releases/de/german-distribution-joint-venture-cfp-brands |access-date=2023-06-01 |website=Ricola |language=en}}</ref>

In 1993, the confectionery producer Disch from [[Othmarsingen]] was taken over, which was sold to the investment company Alrupa Finanz Holding in 2015. Disch produces the brands Sportmint and Mocken, which belong to Ricola.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-05-08 |title=Ricola verkauft Süsswarenproduzentin |url=https://www.schweizerbauer.ch/markt-preise/marktmeldungen/ricola-verkauft-suesswarenproduzentin/ |access-date=2023-06-01 |website=Schweizer Bauer |language=de-DE}}</ref>

In 2006, the company put a state-of-the-art candy factory into operation in Laufen<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2006-05-31 |title=Produktionsneubau Ricola AG Laufen |url=https://tectonews.ch/2006/05/31/produktionsneubau-ricola-ag-laufen/ |access-date=2023-06-01 |website=TECTONEWS |language=de-DE}}</ref> and in 2014 the new {{Lang|de|Kräuterzentrum}} production building was put into operation at the same location.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ricola eröffnet neues Kräuterzentrum |url=https://www.bauernzeitung.ch/artikel/landwirtschaft/ricola-eroeffnet-neues-kraeuterzentrum-366785 |access-date=2023-06-01 |website=bauernzeitung.ch |language=de-CH}}</ref> It is made of clay and is the largest clay house in Europe. The construction was developed by the Austrian ceramist and clay building pioneer Martin Rauch, the architects were [[Herzog & de Meuron]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-06-28 |title=Aus Boden gestampft |url=https://www.bernerzeitung.ch/aus-boden-gestampft-721292626083 |access-date=2023-06-01 |website=[[Berner Zeitung]] |language=de}}</ref>

In 2022, the company opened the first Ricola shop in [[Paris]], where customers can also create their own sweets.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-18 |title=Ausgerechnet Franzosen eröffnen den ersten Ricola-Shop |url=https://www.blick.ch/wirtschaft/wer-hats-erfunden-ausgerechnet-franzosen-eroeffnen-den-ersten-ricola-shop-id18065599.html |access-date=2023-06-01 |website=Blick |language=de-CH}}</ref> In March 2023, the company opened its Ricola shop in Laufen, Switzerland.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ricola: The herbal candies are now available in the experience store |date=16 March 2023 |url=https://www.organisator.ch/en/marketing/2023-03-16/ricola-die-kraeuterbonbons-gibts-jetzt-im-erlebnis-shop/}}</ref>

In 2023, Ricola and IP-SUISSE agreed on a long-term partnership for the sustainable cultivation of sugar beets to produce 25,000 tons of sugar annually without the use of fungicides, insecticides, and herbicides.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ricola setzt auf IP-Suisse-Zucker |date=9 August 2023 |url=https://www.foodaktuell.ch/2023/09/08/ricola-setzt-auf-ip-suisse-zucker}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Zucker: Ricola und IP-Suisse gehen süsse Allianz ein |url=https://www.bauernzeitung.ch/artikel/organisationen-firmen/zucker-ricola-und-ip-suisse-gehen-suesse-allianz-ein-488478}}</ref>

In December 2023, Ricola was certified as a [[B Corporation (certification)|B Corporation]] by the non-profit organisation [[B Lab]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ricola Group AG - Certified B Corporation - B Lab Global |url=https://www.bcorporation.net/en-us/find-a-b-corp/company/ricola-group-ag |access-date=2024-07-07 |website=[[B Corporation]]}}</ref>

The company is now managed by Thomas P. Meier as CEO and Felix Richterich as President of the Board. Today, Ricola exports to over 50 countries in Asia, North America and Europe.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ricola.com/en-ch/About-Ricola/Company |title=The Company |work=Ricola |publisher=Ricola AG |accessdate=2015-12-02}}</ref>

==Ingredients==
[[File:Hustenbonbons 01.jpg|thumb|Ricola herbal cough drop]]
While the [[active ingredient]] in most Ricola products is [[menthol]], an important part of Ricola products is the herb mixture. The following herbs are noted as being part of Ricola's classic blend of 13 herbs:<ref name=herbs13>{{cite web |url=http://www.ricola.com/en-ch/World-of-herbs/Ricola-herbology/The-magic-13-herbs |title=The Magic 13 Herbs |publisher=Ricola AG |accessdate=2015-12-02}}</ref>

* [[Sambucus nigra|Elder]] (''Sambucus nigra'')
* [[Marrubium vulgare|Horehound]] (''Marrubium vulgare'')
* [[Malva|Mallow]] (''Malva silvestris'')
* [[Peppermint]] (''Mentha × piperita'')
* [[Common sage|Sage]] (''Salvia officinalis'')
* [[Thyme]] (''Thymus vulgaris'')
* [[Primula veris|Cowslip]] (''Primula veris'')
* [[Pimpinella saxifraga|Burnet]] (''Pimpinella saxifraga'')
* [[Yarrow]] (''Achillea millefolium'')
* [[Althaea officinalis|Marsh mallow]] (''Althaea officinalis'')
* [[Alchemilla|Lady's mantle]] (''Alchemilla vulgaris'')
* [[Veronica officinalis|Speedwell, {{a.k.a.}} veronica]] (''Veronica officinalis'')
* [[Plantago lanceolata|Ripwort plantain]] (''Plantago lanceolata'')

In the US market, ten herbs make up the herbal mixture, three of which are not in the list above.{{why|date=December 2023}} These are [[Tilia|linden flowers]] (''Tilia platyphyllos''), [[wild thyme]] (''Thymus serpyllum'') and [[hyssop]] (''Hyssopus officinalis'').<ref>{{Cite web|title = Ricola Original – Ingredients|url = http://www.ricola.com/en-us/Products/Original#ingredients|website = Ricola|accessdate = 2015-12-06}}</ref>

The company offers over 60 types of herbal sweets that are supplemented with [[Essential oil|essential oils]], [[Flavoring|natural flavourings]], or [[vitamin C]]. All Ricola products are manufactured in [[Laufen, Switzerland|Laufen]], where Ricola produces 7 billion candies a year.<ref name="Ricola-Schweiz">{{Cite web |title=Ricola Herstellung: Natürlich aus der Schweiz |url=https://www.ricola.com/de/ricola/unternehmen/herstellung |access-date=2023-06-01}}</ref> Variants available in Switzerland include Herbs Original, Lemon Balm, Honey Herbs, Orange Mint, Herbs Caramel, Honey Sage, Echinacea Honey Lemon, Cranberry, Mixed Berry, Sage, Elderflower, Glacial Mint, Eucalyptus and Calendula.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kräuterbonbons: Wohltuend für den Hals |url=https://www.ricola.com/de-ch/ricola-produkte/sortiment/bonbons |access-date=2023-06-01}}</ref> 

Sugar-free versions are also available. Since the beginning of 2022, some of their products have been sweetened with [[Steviol glycoside|steviol glycosides]] from the [[stevia]] plant.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2022-05-05 |title=Ricola Group AG: Ricola: Ein starkes 2. Halbjahr nach herausforderndem Start ins 2021 |url=https://www.nachrichten-heute.net/893158-ricola-group-ag-ricola-ein-starkes-2-halbjahr-nach-herausforderndem-start-ins-2021.html |access-date=2023-06-01 |website=nachrichten-heute.net |language=de-DE}}</ref> {{Asof|2023|11}}, the official US Ricola site mentioned their continuing use of [[aspartame]] artificial sweetener in some products, as well as a stevia-sweetened option.<ref name="Ricola-US-FAQ">{{cite web |title=Frequently Asked Questions |url=https://www.ricola.com/en-us/products/service/faq |website=Ricola [US] |publisher=Ricola |access-date=2023-12-04}}</ref>

Ricola products are also [[Gluten-free diet|gluten-free]], [[halal]], and [[Kashrut|kosher]].<ref name="Ricola-US-FAQ"/>

The product range is tailored to each market individually. For example, filled sweets are also available in Germany and North America. All Ricola products are based on the 13-herb mixture. It also contains [[isomalt]], which carries a risk of intestinal distress when consumed in large quantities (above about 20–30 g (1 oz) per day).<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2020-06-22 |title=Genussvolle Kombination: Tradition mit Fortschritt |url=https://www.promarca.ch/genussvolle-kombination-tradition-mit-fortschritt/ |access-date=2023-06-01 |website=Promarca |language=de-DE}}</ref>

==Ricola herb gardens==
Ricola has five display gardens in Switzerland. They are open to the public<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Ricola Kräuterschaugarten |url=https://www.myswitzerland.com/de-ch/erlebnisse/ricola-kraeuterschaugarten-5/ |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=Schweiz Tourismus |language=de}}</ref> and visitors to the herb gardens can learn about the original herbal blend in their natural environment and learn about the cultivation and power of herbs from May to September.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Auf den Spuren der Heilkräuter im Berner Oberland |url=https://www.nau.ch/lifestyle/reisen/auf-den-spuren-der-heilkrauter-im-berner-oberland-65961509 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=Nau |date= 11 July 2021|language=de}}</ref> The gardens are located at the following locations:<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ricola.com/en-ch/World-of-herbs/Ricola-herb-gardens |title=Ricola Herb Gardens |publisher=Ricola AG |accessdate=2015-12-02 |archive-date=2015-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151207082119/http://www.ricola.com/en-ch/World-of-herbs/Ricola-herb-gardens |url-status=dead }}</ref>

* [[Nenzlingen]], near the company headquarters
* [[Trogberg]], a mountain in the [[canton of Solothurn]]
* [[Kandersteg]] in the [[Berner Oberland]]
* [[Zermatt]] in the [[Valais]]
* [[Pontresina]] in the southern part of [[Grisons]]

The herbs used to produce Ricola's cough drops are not cultivated in these gardens, but in natural plantations in the Swiss mountains in accordance with strict organic or [[BioSuisse]] guidelines. Ricola ensures that its cultivation areas are not situated near industrial sites or the road networks to avoid contact with harmful pollutants. Over 100 self-managed farms are under contract to Ricola in the Valais, Emmental, Puschlav and the [[Jura Mountains]], in Central Switzerland and [[Ticino]]. They grow the herbs for Ricola products on an area equivalent to 124 soccer fields.<ref name="Ricola-Schweiz"/> No pesticides, insecticides or herbicides are used in herb cultivation.<ref name=plants>{{cite web |url=http://www.ricola.com/en-ch/World-of-herbs/Cultivation-of-herbs/Plant-care |title=Ricola herb farmers would rather inspect every single leaf individually than use chemical substances to combat insects or other pests. |publisher=Ricola AG |accessdate=2015-12-02}}</ref>

== Ricola Experience Trail Arosa ==
In cooperation with Arosa Tourism, Ricola opened the Ricola Adventure Trail in Arosa in 2021. The {{Convert|3|km|mi|abbr=on|adj=on}} trail, features ten interactive stations where visitors can learn about bees, the cultivation and importance of herbs, and the production of Ricola's herb drops. The trail complements Ricola's five public herb gardens and offers an additional educational experience in the Swiss Alps, combining information about biodiversity, Swiss herb cultivation and the company's history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ricola-Erlebnisweg in Arosa eröffnet |url=https://www.htr.ch/story/tourismus/ricola-erlebnisweg-in-arosa-eroeffnet-31883.html |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=htr.ch |language=de}}</ref>

== Advertising ==
In 1980, the [[jingle]] was introduced for Ricola that is still used today. In the commercials, [[Ramona Pringle]], among others, sings the characteristic "RIII-CO-LAAAAAAA"; in some videos she imitates [[Heidi]].

In 1998 the first videos of the advertising campaign with the slogan {{Lang|de|Wer hat's erfunden?}} ({{Gloss|Who invented it?}}) aired. The ads were filmed in Finland (1998), Australia (1998), England (1999), Mexico (2000), China (2004), Brazil (2004), and Greenland (2008). The actor was Erich Vock.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jung von Matt/Fleet: Ricola in Brasilien |url=https://www.persoenlich.com/kategorie-werbung/ricola-in-brasilien-253440 |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=persoenlich.com |language=en}}</ref>

Since 2013, Ricola has advertised internationally with the [[Swiss German|Swiss-German]] slogan {{Lang|de|Chrüterchraft}} ({{Gloss|herbal power}}). "''{{Lang|de|Chrüterchraft}}'' is a Swiss word. It stands for herbs, for effect and enjoyment. All Ricola values are contained in this one word: the magical mixture of herbs and the Swiss origin, beneficial effect and good taste of our products”, said Felix Richterich, CEO and Chairman of the Board of Directors of Ricola, to [[Blick.ch]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-10-15 |title=Der Zungenbrecher von Ricola |url=https://www.tagesanzeiger.ch/der-zungenbrecher-von-ricola-504563167160 |access-date=2023-06-14 |website=Tages-Anzeiger |language=de}}</ref>

Ricola then launched the "Wish you Well" campaign, which ran from 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Häusermann |first=Thomas |date=2018-10-13 |title="Wish you well»: Ricola verabschiedet sich endgültig von «Chrüterchraft" |url=https://www.werbewoche.ch/de/werbung/kampagnen/2018-10-13/wish-you-well-ricola-verabschiedet-sich-endgultig-von-chruterchraft/ |access-date=2023-06-14 |website=Werbewoche m&k |language=de-DE}}</ref> In autumn 2021, it was replaced by the new advertising campaign "Just take Ricola", which has since been broadcast across Europe. "With the new advertising campaign, we wanted to focus on what makes Ricola special: naturally grown alpine herbs, the Swiss origin of our company and the balance between enjoyment and functionality of the products. These are the cornerstones of Ricola's success and we will continue to build on them in the future. And as our commercial makes it clear, a pinch of humor plays an important role at Ricola", said Thomas P. Meier, CEO of Ricola, to {{Lang|de|Werbewoche}}.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Willi |first=Sarah |date=2021-11-02 |title=Ricola: Neue Kampagne und neuer Claim «Nimm einfach Ricola» |url=https://www.werbewoche.ch/de/werbung/kampagnen/2021-11-02/ricola-neue-kampagne-und-neuer-claim-nimm-einfach-ricola/ |access-date=2023-06-14 |website=Werbewoche m&k |language=de-DE}}</ref> The advertising campaign also included a revision of the packaging and the logo.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2021-09-29 |title=Rriiiicola: Neues Logo und Packungsdesign {{!}} W&V |url=https://www.wuv.de/Archiv/Rriiiicola-Neues-Logo-und-Verpackungsdesign |access-date=2023-06-14 |website=www.wuv.de |language=de}}</ref>

=== Consumer deception lawsuit ===
In 2022, Ricola was sued in the US for deceiving consumers. The plaintiff claimed that the packaging implied that Swiss herbs would soothe a sore throat, when in fact menthol was the only ingredient with this effect. The accuser requested US$5 million in damages. Ricola, on the other hand, claimed that it had "correctly complied with all regulations at all times".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-23 |title=Ricola wegen falscher Versprechen vor Gericht |url=https://www.blick.ch/wirtschaft/kundin-will-5-millionen-ricola-steht-in-den-usa-wegen-falscher-versprechen-vor-gericht-id17515148.html |access-date=2023-06-14 |website=Blick |language=de-CH}}</ref> The motion was dismissed in 2024 for lack of subject matter jurisdiction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Davis v. Ricola USA, Inc., 3:22-cv-03071 - CourtListener.com |url=https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/63294874/davis-v-ricola-usa-inc/ |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=CourtListener |language=en-us}}</ref>
